Subject: Pilot SLA baseline and credit expectations

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profiles looked promising. Procurement is building our pilot SOW and they have two asks on SLA:

1) Baseline uptime: they are pushing for a 99.9% monthly availability commitment for the pilot (we understand Redwood typically publishes higher numbers, but this is what legal is comfortable with for a short pilot).
2) Monthly remedy cap: they want the monthly service credit to never exceed 5% of the monthly bill for any single month (they're sensitive to credit waterfall exposure).

Also: they asked for explicit maintenance windows / carveouts and a short formula for how credits are calculated so we can attach it to our internal purchase order. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept 99.9 for a pilot and keep credits capped at 5%? If not, what alternate structure would you propose that balances both sides?

Appreciate a quick outline so we can keep momentum.

Best,
Sarah White
Director, SaaS Operations
Optivio

Hi Sarah — thanks, glad the demo was useful. Wanted to give a concrete option so your procurement can move forward:

Option A (Redwood standard):
- Commitment: 99.95% monthly availability
- Remedy: tiered monthly credits measured as a percentage of monthly invoice:
  - 99.95% - 99.90%: 3% credit
  - 99.90% - 99.50%: 10% credit
  - <99.50%: 25% credit
- Scheduled maintenance: up to 6 hours/month, mutually agreed, excluded from uptime calculation

Option B (Pilot middle-ground):
- Commitment: 99.90% for a defined 3-month pilot
- Remedy: capped credit for any month at 6% of that month’s bill (hard cap) with the following trigger bands:
  - 99.90% - 99.75%: 2% credit
  - 99.75% - 99.50%: 6% credit (then capped at 6%)
  - <99.50%: escalation to engineering + one-time remediation credit (outside capped band)
- Scheduled maintenance: up to 8 hours/month for pilot (we'll provide 72h advance notice for planned maintenance)

Rationale: Option B lets us match your procurement comfort on baseline while limiting exposure to our ops economics during a pilot. It also keeps a clear path back to our standard commitments after the pilot. I attached a redline (optivio_sla_redline_v2.docx) and a simple credit calculator so your team can see numeric examples.

If you prefer, we can accept 99.90% for the pilot but ask for a mutual review after month 2 with the option to revert to 99.95 if utilization/latency patterns are stable. Please let me know which route you want and whether Contracts wants different language on carveouts.

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi

Also suggest adding a clause that emergency maintenance (security patches) within a 48h window is carveout if we notify and provide rollback options.

Also call out that remediation credits beyond the cap should require mutually-agreed root cause analysis (avoid unilateral escalation payouts). If legal will need to see that language, loop in Contracts early.

Happy to sync 15m if you want to negotiate live.

Sarah — following an internal review, here’s a final compromise we can commit to for the 3-month pilot:

Final pilot terms (agreed):
- Baseline: 99.90% monthly availability for the 3-month pilot period (Aug–Oct 2026).
- Remedy: tiered credits with a firm cap of 4.5% of monthly invoice for any single month. Trigger bands:
  - 99.90% - 99.80%: 2% credit
  - 99.80% - 99.50%: 4.5% credit (capped)
  - <99.50%: expedited remediation plan + potential one-time makegood negotiated outside normal cap (requires RCA and joint sign-off)
- Maintenance carveouts: up to 8 hours/month scheduled maintenance (72h notice). Emergency security fixes are carveouts with 24–48h notice where feasible; we will provide an incident report and rollback options.
- Review: automatic pilot review after month 2 to consider migrating to Redwood standard 99.95% or adjusting credit bands.

Next steps: I’ve uploaded the redline to DocuSign (link above) — Contracts should review the exact wording around RCA and the makegood clause. If that looks good, we can sign and have the pilot SOW attached.

If Optivio needs the credit-calculator run against a sample monthly invoice, tell me the expected pilot spend and I’ll share numbers from the attached spreadsheet.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you started.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
